source.title: Afghanistan Partial Threat Assessment Map: February 23, 2016

map.title_on_map: AFGHANISTAN PARTIAL THREAT ASSESSMENT AS OF FEBRUARY 23, 2016
map.subtitle: Afghanistan-Pakistan Administrative Divisions, February 2012
map.geographic_extent: Afghanistan and Pakistan with portions of Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, China, and India
map.cartographer: Caitlin Forrest and Rob Denaburg with Harleen Gambhir
map.caption_text: This map partially depicts areas of Taliban and ISIS control and support across Afghanistan as of February 23, 2016. The map also illustrates the status of district centers that have been attacked by Taliban militants in 2015 and 2016. High-confidence ISIS support zones represent areas with reliable reporting of ISIS presence at the sub-district level. Low-confidence ISIS support zones represent areas with reliable reporting of ISIS presence at the district level, with zones assessed based on terrain and historic militant presence, or areas with unconfirmed reporting of ISIS presence at the sub-district level.

1. ANSF retook Ghormach District Center, Baghdis Province from Taliban militants.

4*. Security forces moved government offices to a safer location in Qal'ah-ye Zal District, Kunduz Province after Taliban militants seized the district center's bazaar on February 3.
5. Taliban militants reportedly control schools in Kunduz Province.

8. ISIS's Wilayat Khorasan expanded its presence in Ghazni, Paktika, and Logar Provinces.
9. ANSF retook Reg-e Khan Neshin District Center, Helmand Province from Taliban militants on December 18.
10. Taliban militants have besieged the ANSF in Sangin and Marjah District Centers.
11. Taliban militants contested control of Gereshk, the district center of Nahr-e Saraj District, Helmand Province.
12. Taliban militants contested control of Washer District Center, Helmand Province.
